anatomy.name: Right atrium
anatomy.location: An upper chamber on the right side of the heart. It receives blood returning from the body through the superior and inferior vena cava.
anatomy.function: It collects oxygen-poor blood from the body and passes it through the tricuspid valve to the right ventricle.
anatomy.plain_explanation: Think of the right atrium as a receiving chamber. It gathers blood coming back from the body and guides it toward the lungs.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: An abnormal rhythm or a hole between the upper chambers can change how electrical signals or blood move through the heart.

anatomy.name: Left atrium
anatomy.location: The upper chamber on the left side of the heart. It receives blood returning from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.
anatomy.function: It moves oxygen-rich blood through the mitral valve into the left ventricle, which pumps blood to the body.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The left atrium receives blood that has picked up oxygen in the lungs, then passes it to the heart’s main pumping chamber for the body.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: An abnormal rhythm or a leaky mitral valve can disrupt its coordinated work or place extra volume and pressure on the chamber.

anatomy.name: Right ventricle
anatomy.location: One of the two lower chambers of the heart, on the right side.
anatomy.function: It receives blood from the right atrium through the tricuspid valve and pumps it through the pulmonary valve and pulmonary artery to the lungs.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The right ventricle is the pump that sends blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: If pumping weakens, blood may back up in veins and fluid may build up in body tissues.

anatomy.name: Left ventricle
anatomy.location: The lower chamber on the left side of the heart. It receives blood from the left atrium.
anatomy.function: It pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve into the aorta and onward to the body.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The left ventricle is the heart’s main outgoing pump. It sends blood from the lungs out to the body with each heartbeat.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: Weak or stiff pumping can reduce blood flow to the body or allow pressure to back up toward the lungs.

anatomy.name: Tricuspid valve
anatomy.location: Between the right atrium and right ventricle. It normally has three leaflets, or flaps.
anatomy.function: It opens to let blood move into the right ventricle and closes as the ventricle pumps to limit backward flow.
anatomy.plain_explanation: This three-flap valve is a one-way doorway between the two right-hand heart chambers.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: A narrowed opening can restrict forward flow; a leaky valve lets some blood move backward. Effects vary with severity.

anatomy.name: Pulmonary valve
anatomy.location: At the outlet of the right ventricle, between that chamber and the pulmonary trunk, which leads toward the lungs.
anatomy.function: It opens as the right ventricle contracts to let blood flow toward the lungs, then closes to limit backward flow.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The pulmonary valve is a one-way gate between the heart’s lower-right chamber and the artery leading to the lungs.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: Narrowing can restrict flow to the lungs; leakage can send blood back into the right ventricle.

anatomy.name: Mitral valve
anatomy.location: Between the left atrium and left ventricle. It normally has two leaflets.
anatomy.function: It opens to let blood pass into the left ventricle, then closes as the ventricle pumps to help prevent backward flow.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The mitral valve is a one-way door between the two left-side heart chambers. It helps keep blood moving forward.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: Narrowing restricts forward flow; a leak sends some blood backward. A bulging leaflet (prolapse) does not always cause symptoms.

anatomy.name: Aortic valve
anatomy.location: Between the left ventricle and the aorta, the large artery that carries blood from the heart to the body. It usually has three leaflets.
anatomy.function: It opens when the left ventricle pumps so blood can enter the aorta, then closes to limit backward flow into the ventricle.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The aortic valve is a one-way doorway between the heart’s main pumping chamber and the body’s largest artery.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: Narrowing can limit blood leaving the heart; leakage can send some blood back into the left ventricle.

anatomy.name: Aorta
anatomy.location: The aorta begins at the left ventricle, rises and curves through the chest, then travels down through the chest and abdomen. Its branches supply the body.
anatomy.function: It carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the body through its branches.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The aorta is the main route blood takes out of the heart. Smaller arteries branch from it to carry blood to body tissues.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: A weakened wall can bulge or split and may affect blood flow. Some aortic problems have few early signs.

anatomy.name: Pulmonary artery
anatomy.location: The main pulmonary artery begins at the right ventricle and divides into branches that travel to the right and left lungs.
anatomy.function: It carries oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs, where blood releases carbon dioxide and takes up oxygen.
anatomy.plain_explanation: This artery takes blood from the heart to the lungs so it can pick up oxygen. Unlike most arteries, it carries oxygen-poor blood.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: High pressure in lung arteries can make it harder for blood to pass and make the right ventricle work harder.

anatomy.name: Pulmonary veins
anatomy.location: They run from the lungs to the left atrium. Most people have four major pulmonary veins, two from each lung.
anatomy.function: They carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs to the left atrium. Blood then moves to the left ventricle and is pumped to the body.
anatomy.plain_explanation: After blood picks up oxygen in the lungs, the pulmonary veins bring it back to the heart’s left upper chamber.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: Narrowing or blockage can slow blood returning from the lungs; an unusual connection can change its route.

anatomy.name: Superior vena cava
anatomy.location: A large vein in the chest formed where the right and left brachiocephalic veins meet. It empties into the right atrium and returns blood from above the diaphragm.
anatomy.function: It brings oxygen-poor blood from the head, neck, arms and upper chest back to the heart.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The superior vena cava is a major return route from the upper half of the body to the heart.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: A blockage can slow blood returning from the upper body and may cause swelling or other symptoms.

anatomy.name: Inferior vena cava
anatomy.location: The inferior vena cava forms in the abdomen, travels upward along the right side of the spine, passes through the diaphragm and empties into the right atrium.
anatomy.function: It returns oxygen-poor blood from the lower body and abdomen to the heart.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The inferior vena cava is the main return vein for blood from below the diaphragm. It carries that blood back to the heart.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: A blockage or pressure from nearby structures can slow return from the lower body and sometimes cause leg swelling.

anatomy.name: Interventricular septum
anatomy.location: The muscular and membranous wall between the heart’s right and left ventricles.
anatomy.function: It separates the two lower chambers so blood can follow the usual paths: the right ventricle pumps toward the lungs and the left pumps toward the body.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The interventricular septum is the wall between the heart’s two pumping chambers. It helps keep their blood flows separate.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: A hole between the ventricles can let blood pass between them. Its effects depend on size and location.

anatomy.name: Coronary arteries
anatomy.location: The right and left coronary arteries begin near the root of the aorta and branch over and into the heart muscle.
anatomy.function: They deliver oxygen-rich blood and nutrients to the heart muscle, helping it contract and pump blood.
anatomy.plain_explanation: The coronary arteries are the heart muscle’s own blood supply. They carry oxygen the heart needs to keep pumping.
anatomy.when_it_does_not_work: A narrowed or blocked coronary artery can reduce blood supply to the heart muscle; a severe blockage can cause a heart attack.

circulation.title: Normal blood-flow path through the heart, lungs and body
circulation.overview: The heart moves blood in a repeating loop: body → right side of the heart → lungs → left side of the heart → body. Oxygen-poor blood has less oxygen after body tissues have taken it up; oxygen-rich blood has gained oxygen in the lungs. These labels describe oxygen content, not clean versus dirty blood.
circulation.pulmonary_circulation: Pulmonary circulation carries oxygen-poor blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, where it releases carbon dioxide and takes up oxygen. Oxygen-rich blood then returns to the left side of the heart.
circulation.systemic_circulation: Systemic circulation carries oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle through the aortic valve and aorta to body tissues. After those tissues take up oxygen, oxygen-poor blood returns through veins to the right side of the heart.

steps.title: Oxygen-poor blood returns from the body
steps.description: After body tissues use oxygen, blood returns toward the heart through veins, including the superior and inferior vena cava.
steps.oxygen_status: Oxygen-poor relative to blood returning from the lungs

steps.title: Blood enters the right atrium
steps.description: The superior and inferior vena cava empty oxygen-poor blood into the heart’s upper-right chamber.

steps.title: Blood passes to the right ventricle
steps.description: Blood moves through the tricuspid valve from the right atrium into the lower-right chamber.

steps.title: Blood travels to the lungs
steps.description: The right ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary valve and pulmonary artery toward the lungs. This artery carries oxygen-poor blood.

steps.title: Blood exchanges gases in the lungs
steps.description: In tiny vessels around the lung air sacs, blood takes up oxygen and releases carbon dioxide. Its oxygen status changes from oxygen-poor to oxygen-rich.

steps.title: Oxygen-rich blood returns to the heart
steps.description: Pulmonary veins carry oxygen-rich blood from the lungs back to the heart.

steps.title: Blood enters the left atrium
steps.description: The pulmonary veins empty oxygen-rich blood into the heart’s upper-left chamber.

steps.title: Blood passes to the left ventricle
steps.description: Blood moves through the mitral valve into the lower-left chamber.

steps.title: Blood is pumped out to the body
steps.description: The left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood through the aortic valve into the aorta and its branches, which carry it to body tissues. After tissues take up oxygen, blood returns to the heart through veins.
steps.oxygen_status: Oxygen-rich as it leaves the heart
